# Intervals MCP Server: capability reference

<!-- Generated from apps/server/skills/ by apps/server/src/capabilityReference.test.ts. Do not edit this file: edit the skills, then run UPDATE_CAPABILITY_REFERENCE=1 bunx vitest run src/capabilityReference.test.ts in apps/server. -->

This file is the server's skills in one document: what each tool answers,
the usual sequence of calls, and the rules for reading the numbers and for
the writes.

- A client that supports skills over MCP (Claude and Claude Code) loads
  these skills from the server when a task needs them. It needs nothing from
  this file.
- For a client without skills, upload this file as project knowledge in a
  Claude project that is connected to the server.

The server also sends a short version to every chat as its MCP
instructions: the routing, the id format, units and time zone, and the rules
for the write tools. The full per-tool schemas are in [tools.md](tools.md).

## Contents

- **Reading intervals.icu data** (skill `reading-intervals-data`): Use for the basics behind any answer from this intervals.icu server. Covers finding an activity id, the input names, which unit a number is in, which view tool opens a chart and how to change a chart that is open, why a chart has gaps, and why a change made on intervals.icu does not show here yet.
- **Analysing a run** (skill `run-analysis`): Use to analyse one activity or to compare two. Covers the run summary, laps, splits, hills, intervals, aerobic decoupling, running dynamics, time in zones, raw streams and weather, which tool to call first and which analysis fits which session, and how to read moving time, zone bounds, other sports and similar sessions.
- **Fitness, load and racing** (skill `fitness-and-racing`): Use for questions about fitness, fatigue and form, weekly training load and volume spikes, training totals, best efforts, race predictions and goal paces, tapers, heart rate zones and thresholds, and recovery (HRV, resting heart rate, sleep). Covers the weekly review, race readiness and injury check, and the rule for whole-body versus run-only numbers.
- **Planning and changing routes** (skill `route-planning`): Use to plan where the athlete should run, or to build, change, save, map or export a route. Covers route suggestions from past runs and generated routes, stitched routes, amending a stored route by version, saved running corridors, route maps and GPX or GeoJSON files.
- **Changing the athlete's intervals.icu data** (skill `activity-writes`): Use before you change the athlete's intervals.icu data with update-activity, update-wellness or update-gear. Covers renaming or annotating a run, setting its gear, RPE or feel, logging soreness, fatigue, mood or a niggle for a day, adding or resetting a shoe-mileage reminder, and retiring gear. Says how to confirm the change, which mode keeps existing text, and what to do when a write may already have applied.

## Reading intervals.icu data

This server connects you to one athlete's intervals.icu account:

- activity history, wellness, and the fitness and fatigue trend
- detailed run analysis: hills, splits, intervals, aerobic decoupling and
  race prediction
- route planning from the athlete's own runs
- three write tools: change an activity's name, description, gear, RPE or
  feel; log how the athlete feels on a day; and retire gear or set its
  mileage reminders

Read tools give numbers with explicit units, and they flag missing or
unclear data rather than guess. The write tools never claim that a change
happened when they are not sure. Several tools have a matching interactive
chart (an MCP App) for the same data.

### Finding things

| Tool | Answers | Key inputs |
| ---- | ------- | ---------- |
| `list-activities` | What did I do recently? What is this activity's id? When did I last do X? Each entry has `tags`, `race` and `achievement_types` (a best or a threshold rise) | `oldest`/`newest` (YYYY-MM-DD, default the last 28 days), `type` (`runs` for Run/TrailRun/VirtualRun, one type, or a comma list), `nameContains`, `search` (all history: a name substring or `#tag`), `limit` |
| `get-activity` | Full detail on one activity: gear name, swim pace per 100 m, HR recovery, and any best or threshold rise intervals.icu marked (an LTHR_UP is its estimate, not a changed setting; for a run PB, use `get-best-efforts`) | `id` |
| `list-gear` | What shoes or bikes do I have, their mileage, reminders and auto-assign rules? | `includeRetired` |
| `get-wellness` | HRV, resting HR, sleep, weight, CTL/ATL/TSB and how I felt, for a day or a range | `date`, or `oldest`/`newest` (up to 366 days; past 90 days it gives weekly averages without CTL/ATL/TSB, ramp, sleep score, SpO2, respiration or comments) |

### Activity ids

- Ids are digit strings, optionally with an `i` prefix, as
  `list-activities` gives them (`i189807578`).
- For the most recent run, pass id `"latest"` to a per-activity tool.
  `update-activity` does not take `"latest"`.
- Always pass an id as a quoted string, never as a bare number. Some hosts
  round large numbers through JSON, and that silently changes the id.
- A chart or map opened with `"latest"` stays on that run when the chat is
  opened again. The resolved id is in the result's `_meta`, which the host
  can read but usually does not pass on. When you need the id itself, call
  `list-activities`.

### Input names

The inputs use one camelCase scheme:

- `id` for one activity, `activityId1` and `activityId2` for two.
- `days` for a look-back window (`view-cadence-trends`: 7 to 728, default
  42).
- `newest` to end a look-back on a past date (`get-training-load`,
  `get-fitness-trend` and their charts).

Older spellings (`activity_id`, `weeks`) still work.

### Charts

A view tool opens an interactive chart in the client. Each view tool has a
data tool that the chart itself calls. The data tools are for the charts
only and are not in your tool list: for the same numbers as text, use the
matching read tool (for example `get-fitness-trend` or `get-training-load`).

| View tool | Data tool | Shows |
| --------- | --------- | ----- |
| `view-activity-chart` | `get-activity-streams-raw` | HR, power, pace, altitude, cadence, grade and dynamics overlays, with interval bands |
| `view-cadence-trends` | `get-cadence-trend-data` | Cadence over time: timeline, scatter, zones and overlay views |
| `view-route-map` | `get-route-map-data` | A GPS track with start and finish markers and optional waypoints. With `id`, `from_km` and `to_km`, only that part of a run, to check it before you save a corridor. With `route_id`, a stored route with a colour per section, km markers, via points, `compare_to_version`, and edits on the map (each one an `amend-route` call). A client without MCP Apps gets a picture |
| `view-route-suggestions` | `get-route-suggestions-data` | Past and new routes for a planned run, with a picker, an elevation strip and any hill for repeats |
| `view-training-load` | `get-training-load-data` | Weekly volume bars with a trend line and volume-spike weeks, a weekly load line, and Fitness/Fatigue/Form tiles. `runOnly` picks the starting scope, and the chart toggles between whole body and runs only. `newest` shows a past block |
| `view-compare-activities` | `get-compare-activities-data` | Two activities' streams overlaid, with a delta summary |
| `view-activity-zones` | `get-activity-zones-data` | Time in zone as bars, for HR and, for a run, pace zones |
| `view-fitness-trend` | `get-fitness-trend-data` | CTL/ATL/TSB over time with fatigue and freshness bands, and a taper plan or a calendar plan projection (`calendarPlan`). It toggles between whole body and runs only. `newest` shows a past block, with no projection |
| `view-wellness` | `get-wellness-trend-data` | HRV, resting HR and sleep on one date axis, with gaps where nothing was recorded. `oldest`/`newest` (default the last 30 days); weekly averages past 90 days |

When a chart is open, change it with that chart's own tool. Each reply says
what the card now shows.

- `set-brush-window`: the activity chart zooms to a stretch.
- `set-viewport`: the route map frames a stretch by km.
- `set-view`: cadence trends picks the view, the runs to overlay (by
  `list-activities` id) and the axis.
- `set-metric`: compare activities picks the metric and the axis.
- `set-scope`: fitness trend and training load pick whole body or runs only,
  and which series show.
- `set-zone-type`: activity zones picks heart rate or pace.

Every view tool's text carries the chart's numbers, so you do not need
another call for them. The text is the matching text tool's own text (for
example `get-fitness-trend` for `view-fitness-trend`), from the same call.

- The route map gives its distance, elevation and waypoints, then the climbs
  from `get-hill-analysis`.
- Cadence trends give each run's cadence, cadence by pace zone (the
  athlete's own Run pace zones from `get-athlete-zones`) and the
  cadence-against-pace slope. Runs under 1 km are left out and counted.

The first line of the text says the chart is shown only when the client said
it renders MCP Apps. Otherwise it says the chart may not show, because some
hosts show the card anyway.

### Gaps in charts are missing data, not zero

A stream with no recorded sample (a dropped HR strap, a watch that does not
record running dynamics all the time) shows as a break in the line, not a
drop to zero. This also happens in the middle of an activity, not only at
the start or end. You see it most on the running-dynamics overlays (ground
contact time, vertical oscillation).

### More detail

- Units (below): pace, distance, heart rate, load and the
  `units` object.
- Pacing and caching (below): why a large request takes
  longer, and how long a change made on intervals.icu takes to show here.

### Pacing and caching

The server paces its own calls to intervals.icu, at about one request every
200 ms, because intervals.icu sends no rate-limit headers to react to. A
request that pulls several pieces of data can take a moment longer than a
single lookup. This is normal pacing, not an error.

Reads are cached for a short time, so the same data is not fetched again:

| Data | Cached for |
| ---- | ---------- |
| Activity detail, streams and intervals, and gear | 10 minutes |
| Sport settings | 1 hour (every group at once, as `get-athlete-zones` reads them: 10 minutes) |
| Activity list | 1 minute |
| Wellness | 5 minutes |
| Pace and heart rate curves | 10 minutes |

After a write, the server clears the entries the write changed:

- `update-activity` clears that activity and the related list and gear
  entries.
- `update-wellness` clears the wellness entries.
- `update-gear` clears the gear list.

So a read after the write (for example `get-activity`) shows the change at
once. Everything else stays on its normal schedule. A change made outside
this chat, directly on intervals.icu, can take up to the time above to show
here.

### Units

- **Pace** for a run is a bare `m:ss` string per kilometre, in a
  `*_min_per_km` field (`pace_min_per_km`, `gap_min_per_km`,
  `avg_pace_min_per_km`), never miles. Where a tool also needs the number
  for arithmetic, it adds a paired `*_sec_per_km` field in seconds
  (`get-race-prediction`'s `pace_sec_per_km`, `compare-activities`'
  `pace_delta_sec_per_km`).
- A swim's pace is per 100 m, in `pace_min_per_100m` (`units.swim_pace`).
  Other sports get `speed_kmh` (`units.speed`). `get-athlete-zones` also
  gives a swim group's paces per 100 m, in `*_min_per_100m` fields.
- **The `units` object.** Most tool responses include a `units` object that
  names the unit of every field (distance, HR, cadence in spm or rpm, HRV in
  ms, SpO2 in %, respiration in breaths/min), so a unit is never implied.
- **Distance** is in metres or kilometres, named per field.
  `get-race-prediction` gives distance in metres (`units.distance: "m"`,
  `distance_m` fields).
- **Heart rate** is in beats per minute.
- **Load** is intervals.icu's own training-load unit
  (`icu_training_load`), summed or averaged per day or week, depending on
  the tool.

## Analysing a run

### Start with the summary

Call `get-running-summary` first for the overall picture. Then call the one
analysis that fits what the run was:

| The run was | Call |
| ----------- | ---- |
| A workout with structured reps | `get-interval-analysis`, with `findSimilar: true` to compare with earlier sessions of the same reps |
| A steady run on a mostly flat course | `get-split-analysis` |
| Hilly for its distance | `get-hill-analysis` |
| A long, easy, steady run | `get-aerobic-analysis`, for decoupling |

For other sports, use `get-activity`. The `run-debrief` prompt runs this
sequence, and adds that day's wellness from `get-wellness`.

### Per-activity detail

| Tool | Answers | Key inputs |
| ---- | ------- | ---------- |
| `get-running-summary` | One readout for a run: metrics, HR zones, cadence, dynamics, laps, weather (with humidity and dew point when the FIT file has them), and decoupling and efficiency factor (computed from the streams when intervals.icu has none) | `id` |
| `get-activity-laps` | What were the lap splits? | `id`, `fromLap` |
| `get-running-dynamics` | Ground contact time, vertical oscillation and ratio, step length | `id`, `includeIntervals`, `fromLap` |
| `get-activity-zones` | Time in each HR zone and, for a run, each pace zone (GAP when the activity uses it). Power zones are not reported yet | `id` |
| `get-activity-streams` | Raw time series (HR, pace, cadence, power, altitude, corrected altitude and more) | `id`, `types`, `maxPoints` |

### Per-activity analysis

| Tool | Answers | Key inputs |
| ---- | ------- | ---------- |
| `get-hill-analysis` | How did the climbs go, and did I fade on them late? | `id`, `elevationSource` (`corrected` by default, `barometric`, or `both` for each source's climbs side by side) |
| `get-split-analysis` | Did I positive-split, or was that the hills? | `id`, `elevationSource` |
| `get-aerobic-analysis` | Did I decouple? What is my efficiency factor? | `id`, `basis` (`gap`, `pace` or `power`; `gap` corrects for hills), `elevationSource` (`both` shows decoupling on each elevation source and warns when they disagree) |
| `get-interval-analysis` | Pace and HR per rep, and did the reps fade? Am I faster than the last times I did this workout? | `id`, `findSimilar` |
| `compare-activities` | How does this run compare with that one? Was the gap there from km 1 (conditions) or did it grow (fatigue)? Was the weather different? Am I getting faster on my usual loop? | `activityId1` and `activityId2`, or `activityId1` with `sameRoute: true` |

### Rules for reading the numbers

#### Three moving times, each labelled

intervals.icu's moving time for the activity (`get-activity`,
`get-running-summary`, `compare-activities`), the streams' moving time with
stops left out (`get-split-analysis` and the other stream tools; it matches
the watch's own timer), and intervals.icu's moving time per lap can differ by
tens of seconds on one run. So the paces differ by a few seconds per km.
Each pace's `moving_time_source` says which one it is (`intervals.icu`,
`streams` or `lap`). Quote the one that fits the question, and say which.

#### Two sources of zone bounds

`get-athlete-zones` gives today's sport settings. `get-activity-zones` and
`get-running-summary` use the bounds recorded with each activity, which can
be older. HR zone tools need the activity's own recorded zone bounds or a
matching Run sport-settings group. Without either, the HR zone data is empty
rather than wrong.

#### Other sports

- Pace fields (`pace_min_per_km`, `gap_min_per_km`) are filled only for
  Run, TrailRun and VirtualRun. A Walk or Hike gets cadence and `speed_kmh`
  but no pace, and the charts show it in km/h too.
- A swim gets `pace_min_per_100m` and no running dynamics. `get-activity`
  adds SWOLF and distance per stroke for a swim. Other sports with a
  distance get `speed_kmh`.
- Cadence is doubled to steps/min for Run, TrailRun, VirtualRun, Walk and
  Hike. A swim gives its stroke rate in strokes/min, and other sports give
  the raw rate in rpm (`units.cadence_label`).

#### Weather

Humidity and dew point come from the FIT file (HealthFit writes Apple's
workout weather there). intervals.icu's own weather is empty unless the
athlete's settings fetch it. A temperature from the file can be a watch
sensor's reading, which a wrist warms. When the dew points in
`compare-activities` differ by more than 5 °C, it says so: part of the
heart rate difference can be the weather.

#### Similar sessions are found from laps

`get-interval-analysis` with `findSimilar: true` compares only earlier
sessions whose laps show clean reps. A workout with no lap per rep (1 km
auto-laps only) is skipped and counted in `skipped`, not found. An empty
`sessions` list always comes with a `reason`. Quote it, rather than saying
the athlete never did the workout.

#### Strava stubs

An activity synced into intervals.icu from Strava with no further detail is
flagged (`is_strava_stub`). Do not expect streams or laps for it.

## Fitness, load and racing

### Tools

| Tool | Answers | Key inputs |
| ---- | ------- | ---------- |
| `get-fitness-trend` | Am I fresh or fatigued? What if I taper for a race? | `days`, `newest`, `runOnly`, `projectDays`/`plannedLoads`/`calendarPlan`, `targetDate`/`targetTsb` |
| `get-training-load` | Weekly volume, volume-spike flags, long run, HR zone split, weekly load | `days`, `newest`, `runOnly` |
| `get-athlete-stats` | Run totals with the longest run, and totals for every sport (strength sessions, swim distance), for this week, month and year to date, last year to date, and any date range | `oldest`, `newest` (an optional range) |
| `get-best-efforts` | My best mile, 5K, 10K, half and marathon times, or grade-adjusted bests; my fastest 100 m or 1500 m swim; my fastest 5K inside one run, and where; how my 5K best and critical speed moved by month, quarter or year | `distances`, `window`, `topN`, `gap`, `sport`, `id`, `progression` |
| `get-race-prediction` | What could I run for X? What pace do I need for a goal time? | `raceDistance` (`5km`, `10km`, `15km`, `10 mile`, `half marathon`, `marathon`, `50km`), `goalTime` |
| `get-athlete-zones` | What are my HR zones? Is 150 bpm zone 2? What is my threshold pace? Is my LTHR out of date? | `sport` (default Run) |
| `get-wellness` | HRV, resting HR, sleep, soreness and how I felt, for a day or a range | `date`, or `oldest`/`newest` |

For a chart of the same numbers, use `view-fitness-trend`,
`view-training-load` or `view-wellness`.

### Whole-body versus run-only numbers

- `get-fitness-trend` and `get-training-load` give whole-body CTL/ATL/TSB
  by default. They read it from intervals.icu's own wellness record, which
  covers every activity type.
- `runOnly: true` gives a separate series that the server computes from
  Run, TrailRun and VirtualRun only.
- The two can give very different numbers for the same athlete, and they
  answer different questions. Do not mix them in one comparison, and say
  which one each number is.
- `get-athlete-stats` gives both side by side: run totals with run-only
  load, and `all_sports` with whole-body load.

### Workflows

#### Weekly review

1. `get-training-load` for volume, trend, warnings, the weekly
   easy/moderate/hard split and each week's long run.
2. `list-activities` to find the hardest efforts.
3. `get-running-summary` on those runs (and `compare-activities` for two
   comparable runs).
4. `view-cadence-trends` to explore cadence patterns.

The `weekly-review` prompt runs this sequence.

#### Race readiness

- `get-fitness-trend` with `targetDate` and `targetTsb` for race-day form
  and the taper, plus `calendarPlan` for where form lands if the athlete
  follows the workouts planned on the intervals.icu calendar.
- `get-race-prediction` for the time.
- `get-wellness` for the last 7 days.
- `get-training-load` for recent load.

The `race-readiness` prompt runs this sequence.

#### Injury check

- `get-training-load` volume-spike warnings (a sharp rise on recent volume,
  not an injury measure).
- The HRV and resting-HR trend from `get-wellness`.
- `get-fitness-trend` flags.
- Shoe mileage from `list-gear` (the athlete's own reminders first).

This is training-load guidance, not a diagnosis. The `injury-check` prompt
runs this sequence.

#### Race prediction

Call `get-race-prediction` alone. Pass `raceDistance` for a km split table,
or `goalTime` to pace the splits to a target instead of a prediction. It
uses one pace-curve point per run, and it counts runs marked as races in
intervals.icu twice. So a history of training runs only usually predicts on
the slow side.

#### Fitness and taper planning

- `get-fitness-trend` with `targetDate` and `targetTsb` solves a taper.
- `projectDays`/`plannedLoads` projects forward under an assumed plan.
- `calendarPlan` projects from the workouts planned on the intervals.icu
  calendar.
- `view-fitness-trend` shows the same thing as a chart, with a Whole body /
  Runs only toggle.

`targetDate` must be after today and at most 180 days ahead.

### Rules for reading the numbers

#### Training-load weeks are whole weeks

- `get-training-load` and `view-training-load` round `days` up to whole
  Monday-to-Sunday weeks, and add the current week so far. `days: 28` is
  the last 4 complete weeks plus this week.
- The current week is marked in progress. Averages and the trend leave it
  out, and it gets a warning only for the volume it already has. Do not read
  a short current week as a drop in volume.
- Weeks with no runs count as zero weeks, including a layoff that is still
  going on.
- With `newest` (a past date, never after today), `days` counts back from
  it. A past Sunday ends the window on a complete week (`days: 84` is
  exactly 12 weeks). Any other past date ends it on a partial week, marked
  "partial" and treated like the current week. Then `period.ends_today` is
  false, and `get-fitness-trend` gives no projection or taper for the past
  window.

#### Volume-spike flags compare with the recent average

A week is flagged when its distance is more than 1.5 times the average of
the 4 complete weeks before it. The reason gives the ratio. A normal week
after a recovery or taper week is not flagged. The flag marks a sharp rise,
not a measured injury risk: say so, and do not present it as a diagnosis.

#### The LTHR and max HR check is a hint

A heart rate sensor error can also put a best above a setting, so check the
named activity first. The LTHR check uses intervals.icu's own rule: the
higher of the best 60-minute heart rate and 98% of the best 20-minute heart
rate, over the last 90 days. An estimate below a setting does not mean that
the setting is too high.

## Planning and changing routes

### Tools

| Tool | Answers | Key inputs |
| ---- | ------- | ---------- |
| `suggest-run-route` | Where should I run my planned run? Past runs from that start that fit the distance and terrain, plus a newly generated route, each with a `route_id` to stitch, map or export it. See "How suggestions are chosen" below | `date`, `days`, `distanceKm`, `start`, `end`, `via` (one place or a list, in order), `shape`, `terrain` |
| `stitch-route` | Run my Sunday route, but add a 1 km out-and-back toward Iron Cove at halfway. Joins km ranges of past runs, stored routes, saved corridors, routed sections and out-and-backs into one stored route; gaps over 30 m are routed. Returns a `route_id`, version 1, and each section's km, source, climb and path share | `segments` (`activity`, `route`, `corridor`, `generated`, `out_and_back`), `name` |
| `amend-route` | Move the turnaround 200 m west; go through the park; cut km 3-4; swap a section for a saved corridor (`replace_section` with `corridor`); make it 15 km; undo. Routes only the changed part into a new version, keeps every old one, and says the distance change and the km that changed | `route_id`, `base_version` (must be the latest), `operations` |
| `list-corridors` | Which corridors have I saved near the office? What do I keep running that I have not named? Saved corridors nearest first, and stretches that recent runs repeat; with `through` (one or two places), the recent runs that pass them | `near`, `through` |
| `manage-corridors` | Save km 3-5.4 of Sunday's run as Glebe foreshore; rename it; mark it one-way; re-cut it from another run (`recut`); forget it. A saved corridor can be a `via` in `suggest-run-route`, and a section in `stitch-route` and `amend-route` | `action`, `route_id`, `name`, `one_way`, `activity`, `route` |
| `export-route` | Send me the GPX. A stored route's version, or a past run, as a GPX or GeoJSON file with a waypoint every km | `route_id` + `version`, or `id`; `format`, `waypoints` |

`view-route-suggestions` shows the suggestions on a map with a picker.
`view-route-map` draws a run or a stored route.

### How suggestions are chosen

- The generated route needs `ORS_API_KEY` on the server. Without it, the
  suggestions are past runs and stitched routes only.
- Routes are scored 0 to 100 from a local OpenStreetMap index and the
  athlete's runs: off-road paths, lines the athlete runs often, road
  crossings, main roads, backtracking, green space and fit to the plan. The
  best 3 come back.
- With via points, a route stitched from sections of past runs between them
  is one of the candidates.
- Without via points, when no past run fits the distance, out-and-backs
  along past runs and past loops joined end to end are candidates.
- A via that matches only a suburb or a city is refused. Give `lat,lng` for
  it instead.

### Workflow

1. **Suggest.** `suggest-run-route` (or `view-route-suggestions` for a map)
   with the planned distance and start.
2. **Build.** To combine parts of past runs, stored routes and corridors,
   `stitch-route`. It stores a new route and gives its `route_id`.
3. **Change.** `amend-route` with the route's latest version as
   `base_version`. An older `base_version` is refused, so read the latest
   version from the last result first. Every change is a new version, and
   `undo` goes back.
4. **Check.** `view-route-map` with the `route_id` draws it.
5. **Export.** `export-route` gives the GPX or GeoJSON file as a link.

### Rules

- Results never carry the route's geometry. `export-route` links it as a
  file, and `view-route-map` draws it.
- Each tool call has a budget of routing calls. A stitch that needs more
  stores nothing. An amend that needs more stores nothing and returns
  `applied: false`, a warning and the latest version.
- To save a stretch as a corridor, check it first with `view-route-map`
  with the run's `id`, `from_km` and `to_km`.
- Deleting a corridor cannot be undone. Name the corridor and wait for a yes
  before you call `manage-corridors` with `delete`. A client that can show a
  form also asks the athlete to confirm it.

## Changing the athlete's intervals.icu data

Three tools write to intervals.icu:

| Tool | Changes | Key inputs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update-activity` | One activity's name, description, gear, RPE (1 to 10) or feel (1 to 5) | `id`, `name`, `description`, `descriptionMode`, `gearId`, `rpe`, `feel` |
| `update-wellness` | One day's soreness, fatigue, stress, mood, motivation, injury, sleep quality and comments ("log today: legs sore, left calf tight") | `date`, `soreness`, `fatigue`, `stress`, `mood`, `motivation`, `injury`, `sleepQuality`, `comments`, `commentsMode` |
| `update-gear` | One gear item: retire it, put it back in use, add a distance reminder or reset one ("remind me at 700 km on the new pair; retire the old ones") | `gearId`, one of `retired`, `addReminderKm` (+ `reminderName`), `resetReminderId` |

Everything else this server writes (stored routes and corridors) is in its own
route store, not in intervals.icu.

### Rules for every write

1. **Read first.** Get the current values before you draft a change:
   `get-running-summary` or `get-activity` for an activity, `get-wellness`
   for a day, `list-gear` for gear and reminder ids.
2. **Show the exact change and wait for a yes.** Quote the field, the old
   value and the new value. Do not write on an implied yes. If the athlete
   changes the text, show it again.
3. **Keep the athlete's text.** To add a note, use `descriptionMode: "append"`
   (`update-activity`) or `commentsMode: "append"` (`update-wellness`). Use
   `"replace"` only when the athlete asked to overwrite the text.
4. **Send only what changes.** Leave out every field the athlete did not ask
   to change. The tools also skip a field whose value is already the same.
5. **Report what the reply says changed**, with its before and after values,
   not what you asked for.

### When the host asks the athlete to confirm

On a client with form-mode elicitation, some writes first open a
confirmation in the host: a `replace` that would drop existing text (it
shows the current and the new text), and retiring gear with `update-gear`
(it names the item and its distance). Nothing is sent until the athlete
accepts. If the athlete declines,
nothing changed: say so, and do not send the call again unless they ask.

### When a write may already have applied

Each tool reads the data fresh and sends one write, which is never retried.
If the reply says it cannot tell whether the change landed (the write timed
out, or the confirming re-read failed), **do not send the same call again**.
Re-read with `get-activity`, `get-wellness` or `list-gear`, tell the athlete
what the data shows now, and write again only if the change is not there.

### update-activity

- Get the id from `list-activities`. Pass it as a quoted string
  (`"i189807578"`). `update-activity` does not take `"latest"`: resolve the
  run with `list-activities` first.
- **Annotating a run:** read `get-running-summary` (it has the laps), draft a
  short note from what the data shows, show it, then send it with
  `descriptionMode: "append"`. This is also what the `annotate-last-run`
  prompt does.
- **A description needs a mode when one already exists.** If the activity has
  a description that the new text does not contain, a call with no
  `descriptionMode` writes nothing. The error gives the existing text's
  length and its first 120 characters. Ask the athlete whether to append or
  replace, then resend. After a `replace` that drops text, the reply quotes
  what was removed.
- **Gear can be changed, not cleared.** `gearId` must be an id from
  `list-gear`. intervals.icu ignores a request to set no gear.
- `rpe` is 1 (easiest) to 10 (hardest). `feel` is 1 ("Strong") to 5 (the
  weakest feeling).

### update-wellness

- `date` is YYYY-MM-DD and defaults to today in the configured time zone.
- Turn the athlete's words into the 1 to 4 scores in
  Wellness scores (below). On every
  scale, 1 is the best state. Show the scores you chose before you send them.
- Put free text such as "left calf tight" in `comments`, with
  `commentsMode: "append"` when the day already has comments.
- `null` clears a score. Device values (HRV, resting heart rate, sleep time,
  weight) are never written.
- **A locked day takes no API change.** If the athlete locked the day in
  intervals.icu, the reply warns for each value that was not applied. Tell
  the athlete to unlock the day in intervals.icu, then try again.
  `update-wellness` itself never locks a day, so a device sync later the
  same day still lands.

### update-gear

- `list-gear` shows each item's distance, purchase date, reminders (with
  their ids) and auto-assign rules. Get `gearId` and reminder ids there.
- One change per call: exactly one of `retired`, `addReminderKm` (with an
  optional `reminderName`) or `resetReminderId`. For two changes, make two
  calls, each confirmed.
- `retired: true` retires the item today. Before you retire it, name the item
  and its distance so the athlete can check it is the right pair.
- `addReminderKm` adds a reminder. The reply shows how much usage
  intervals.icu already counts toward it. `resetReminderId` restarts a
  reminder's count from now.
- A reminder with the same name and distance as an existing one is refused,
  so a repeated call adds no duplicate.

### Wellness scores for update-wellness

Every score is an integer from 1 to 4. On every scale, 1 is the best state.
`null` clears a score.

| Field | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `soreness` | low | average | high | extreme |
| `fatigue` | low | average | high | extreme |
| `stress` | low | average | high | extreme |
| `mood` | great | good | OK | grumpy |
| `motivation` | extreme | high | average | low |
| `injury` | none | niggle | poor | injured |
| `sleepQuality` | great | good | average | poor |

#### Turning words into scores

| The athlete says | Send |
| --- | --- |
| "legs are a bit sore" | `soreness: 2` |
| "legs are trashed" | `soreness: 3` or `4`: ask which |
| "slept badly" | `sleepQuality: 4` |
| "left calf is tight" | `injury: 2` and `comments: "left calf tight"` |
| "can't wait to run" | `motivation: 1` |

When a word fits two scores, ask; do not guess. Show the scores and any
comment text before you send them.

#### After logging

`get-wellness` over a range shows when a niggle started. `get-training-load`
for the same weeks shows the load around it.
